mainTopic: צדיקים replacing each other, אגדה about פלטיהו, the lineage of lands, the future purification of ממזרים, and whether a גר may marry a ממזרת
overview: The amud opens with the last words of רבי on the day he died: a baby has just entered אברהם's covenant, and רב יהודה has just been born. From a chain of sages, each born as the previous one died, the גמרא learns that a צדיק never leaves the world before an equal צדיק is created. It gives a second example from עלי and שמואל. Next it explains a פסוק in איכה with the town הומניא, and brings a disagreement between רב and שמואל on whether יחזקאל's cry over פלטיהו בן בניה was 'for good' or 'for bad.' The גמרא tries to prove which view is שמואל's from his statement about the lineage of מישן, but that proof is pushed back using שמואל's rule that an ownerless slave goes free. The גמרא then returns to lineage: שמואל says the משנה follows רבי מאיר, while the חכמים presume all lands are fine, and אמימר relies on this in a real marriage case despite רב אשי's challenge. A ברייתא follows on whether ממזרים will be purified in the future, and the הלכה follows רבי יוסי that they will. Finally, a new ברייתא asks whether a גר may marry a ממזרת, and the explanation of רבי יוסי's reason continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A baby joins אברהם's covenant, and רב יהודה is born
steps.stepSummary: רבי's deathbed words end: today a baby sits in אברהם's lap, and today רב יהודה was born in בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Today he is sitting in the lap of אברהם. Today רב יהודה was born in בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting what רבי said on the day he died. He announces two pieces of good news happening on that very day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Sitting in אברהם's lap' means a baby just had his ברית מילה and joined אברהם's covenant. The second line, that רב יהודה was born today, is the claim the גמרא will support in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The lap of אברהם; here, joining his covenant through ברית מילה

phrases.english: Today he is sitting in the lap of Abraham.
phrases.notes: He means a baby who just had his ברית מילה, which brings him into אברהם's covenant.

phrases.english: Today Rav Yehuda was born in Babylonia.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיּוֹם יוֹשֵׁב בְּחֵיקוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי's deathbed words from the end of the previous section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the day רבי died, a baby entered the covenant and רב יהודה was born.

steps.title: A chain of sages, each born as the one before him died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a teaching that lists great sages, each born when the previous one died.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: When רבי עקיבא died, רבי was born. When רבי died, רב יהודה was born. When רב יהודה died, רבא was born. When רבא died, רב אשי was born.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבי's claim that רב יהודה was born on the day רבי died. It quotes a known teaching that lists a whole chain of such births.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's statement fits inside a larger pattern. From רבי עקיבא down to רב אשי, each new great sage was born just as the earlier one passed away.

keyTerms.meaning: As the Master said; this introduces a known teaching

phrases.english: As the Master said:
When Rabbi Akiva died, Rabbi was born.
phrases.notes: "רבי" here means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: When Rabbi died, Rav Yehuda was born.
When Rav Yehuda died, Rava was born.
When Rava died, Rav Ashi was born.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in Step 1 that רב יהודה was born when רבי died.
steps.raayaObject: רבי's statement that רב יהודה was born on the day he died
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of 'מר' listing a chain of births from רבי עקיבא to רב אשי

steps.title: The lesson: a צדיק leaves only after another is created
steps.stepSummary: From the chain, the גמרא learns that a צדיק does not leave the world until an equal צדיק is created, based on a פסוק in קהלת.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches you that a צדיק does not leave the world until a צדיק like him is created, as it says: 'The sun rises and the sun sets.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the lesson from the chain of births and grounds it in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions the sun rising before it mentions the sun setting. In the same way, the next צדיק's 'sun' rises before the current צדיק's 'sun' sets, so the world is never left without a צדיק.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main idea of the whole section: ה׳ makes sure each generation has its צדיקים.

phrases.aramaic: לְלַמֶּדְךָ שֶׁאֵין צַדִּיק נִפְטָר מִן הָעוֹלָם
phrases.english: To teach you that a righteous person does not leave the world
until a righteous person like him is created,
as it is stated: "The sun rises and the sun sets."
phrases.notes: קהלת 1:5. Notice the rising comes first in the פסוק, before the setting.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְלַמֶּדְךָ שֶׁאֵין צַדִּיק נִפְטָר מִן הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the general lesson from the list in Step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A צדיק is not taken from the world until an equal צדיק has already been created.

steps.title: The same pattern with עלי and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: Another example: שמואל's 'sun' was already shining before עלי's went out, as the פסוק in שמואל shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Before עלי's sun went out, the sun of שמואל הרמתי was already shining, as it says: 'The lamp of God had not yet gone out, and שמואל was lying...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the same rule working in the time of נביאים. It uses a פסוק about עלי and young שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'lamp of God' hints at עלי, who was still alive. At that same time שמואל was already in the משכן and starting his role, so the new leader was in place before the old one passed away.

keyTerms.meaning: His sun went out; he died
It rose; it began to shine
עלי the כהן גדול, leader before שמואל

steps.whatToRemember: Every generation is given new צדיקים before the old ones pass on: רבי עקיבא to רבי, רבי to רב יהודה, and long before that, עלי to שמואל.

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁלֹּא כָּבְתָה שִׁמְשׁוֹ שֶׁל עֵלִי
phrases.english: Before Eli's sun had gone out,
the sun of Samuel the Ramathite was rising,
as it is stated: "And the lamp of God had not yet gone out,
and Samuel was lying, etc."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 3:3. The פסוק goes on: in the היכל of ה׳.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד שֶׁלֹּא כָּבְתָה שִׁמְשׁוֹ שֶׁל עֵלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an earlier example of the rule stated in Step 3.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a צדיק leaves only after another is created
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א 3:3, showing שמואל already active while עלי was still alive

steps.title: Enemies all around: הומניא next to פום נהרא
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains a פסוק in איכה, that Jews are surrounded by enemies, with the example of הומניא beside פום נהרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'ה׳ commanded concerning יעקב that those around him are his enemies.' רב יהודה said: For example, הומניא next to פום נהרא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the town הומניא, which רבי had mentioned earlier. רב יהודה uses it as a real example of the פסוק in איכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says Jews will have enemies living right around them, even in exile. הומניא was an enemy town sitting right next to פום נהרא, a town where Jews lived.

keyTerms.meaning: Those around him are his enemies
A town described earlier as עמוני
A town in בבל with Jewish residents

phrases.english: "The Lord has commanded concerning Jacob that those around him should be his adversaries."
phrases.notes: איכה 1:17.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says:
For example, Homanya next to Pum Nahara.
phrases.notes: הומניא was called an עמוני town a little earlier. פום נהרא, right beside it, had Jews living in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: צִוָּה ה׳ לְיַעֲקֹב סְבִיבָיו צָרָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the town הומניא, mentioned earlier in רבי's deathbed words, after the side point about צדיקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הומניא, an enemy town right beside Jewish פום נהרא, is an example of 'those around יעקב are his enemies.'

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue about פלטיהו's death
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק where יחזקאל cries out when פלטיהו בן בניה dies, רב and שמואל disagree: one reads it for good, one for bad.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And as I prophesied, פלטיהו בן בניה died; I fell on my face, cried out loudly and said: Ah, Lord God!' רב and שמואל: one said it is for good, and one said it is for bad.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק from יחזקאל and reports that רב and שמואל disagree about how to understand it. It is setting up the next step, which explains one of the views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether פלטיהו's death and יחזקאל's cry are meant to be read in a good way or a bad way. The גמרא does not say yet which אמורא holds which view.

keyTerms.meaning: For good; in a positive way
For bad; in a negative way

phrases.english: "And it came to pass when I prophesied, that Pelatiah son of Benaiah died,
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 11:13.

phrases.aramaic: וָאֶפֹּל עַל פָּנַי וָאֶזְעַק קוֹל גָּדוֹל
phrases.english: and I fell upon my face and cried out with a loud voice,
and said: Ah, Lord God!"
Rav and Shmuel disagree:
One said: It is for good,
and one said: It is for bad.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל: חַד אָמַר: לְטוֹבָה, וְחַד אָמַר: לְרָעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new piece of אגדה about a פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב and שמואל disagree whether the פסוק about פלטיהו's death should be read for good or for bad.

steps.title: The 'for good' view begins: the governor of מישן asks for captives
steps.stepSummary: To explain the 'for good' view, the גמרא starts a story: the governor of מישן, נבוכדנצר's son-in-law, complained that he was sent no captives to serve him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says 'for good' explains it like this story: the governor of מישן was נבוכדנצר's son-in-law. He sent him a message: 'Of all the captives you brought for yourself, you did not send us anyone to stand before us?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the 'for good' view through a story. This step only sets up the story, and Step 8 finishes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The governor of מישן was related to נבוכדנצר by marriage. He asks why none of the Jewish captives were sent to serve him, which opens the way for the rest of the story.
steps.confusionAlert: The story is not finished here. Wait for the next lines before deciding how it shows the 'for good' reading.

phrases.english: The one who says it is for good:
it is like that story of the governor of Meishan,
who was the son-in-law of Nebuchadnezzar.
He sent him a message:
From all these captives that you brought for yourself,
you have not sent us anyone to stand before us?
phrases.notes: "To stand before us" means to serve him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר לְטוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the 'for good' view from Step 6 through a story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'for good' view is explained through a story that begins with the governor of מישן asking נבוכדנצר for captives.

steps.title: Pelatiah sends the slaves instead of the nobles
steps.stepSummary: נבוכדנצר wanted to send Jewish captives to his son-in-law. פלטיהו בן בניה convinced him to keep the important Jews with him and send the slaves instead, so the נביא asks: should someone who did such good die young?
steps.simpleTranslation: נבוכדנצר wanted to send him captives from the Jews. פלטיהו בן בניה said to him: 'We important people should stay and serve you here, and let our slaves go there.' And the נביא said: Should a person who did good for Israel die in the middle of his life?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the story it began in Step 7, which explains the 'for good' reading of יחזקאל's cry. פלטיהו saved the important Jews from being sent away, so his early death was a sad loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, יחזקאל's cry over פלטיהו's death is a cry of pain: a man who protected the Jews died before his time. The story also tells us that slaves, not important Jewish families, were sent to מישן. That detail matters later in Step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: in the middle of his life (dying young)
a leader of the people whose death יחזקאל saw

phrases.english: He wanted to send him captives from the Jews.
phrases.notes: 'He' is נבוכדנצר, and 'him' is his son-in-law, the governor of מישן from Step 7.

phrases.english: Pelatiah son of Benaiah said to him:
We, who are important,
should stand before you here,
and our slaves should go there.
And the prophet said:
One who did good for Israel,
should he die in the middle of his days?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי לְשַׁדּוֹרֵי לֵיהּ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story begun in Step 7 that supports the 'for good' reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the 'for good' view, פלטיהו did good by sending slaves to מישן instead of important Jews, so יחזקאל mourned his early death.

steps.title: The 'for bad' view brings two verses
steps.stepSummary: The view that יחזקאל's cry was 'for bad' quotes two פסוקים. The first places פלטיהו among twenty-five men at the Temple gate. The second describes twenty-five men with their backs to the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says 'for bad' points to the פסוק: 'A spirit brought me to the eastern gate of the House of ה׳, and at the gate were twenty-five men, among them יאזניה בן עזור and פלטיהו בן בניה, leaders of the people.' And another פסוק says: 'He brought me to the inner courtyard, and at the entrance of the היכל, between the אולם and the מזבח, were about twenty-five men, their backs to the היכל of ה׳ and their faces to the east.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the source for the other opinion, which says יחזקאל's cry was over a wicked man. This step only quotes the two פסוקים; the next step explains them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים mention a group of twenty-five men, so the group is treated as the same one. The first פסוק names פלטיהו in it, and the second describes what the group did. The second פסוק's odd extra words become the key point in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: for bad (the death was a punishment)
the Sanctuary building of the בית המקדש
the entrance hall in front of the היכל

phrases.english: The one who says 'for bad': as it is written:
"And a spirit brought me to the gate of the House of ה׳,
the eastern one, which faces east;

phrases.aramaic: וְהִנֵּה בְּפֶתַח הַשַּׁעַר עֶשְׂרִים וַחֲמִשָּׁה אִישׁ
phrases.english: and behold, at the entrance of the gate were twenty-five men;

phrases.aramaic: וָאֶרְאֶה בְתוֹכָם אֶת יַאֲזַנְיָה בֶן עַזֻּר
phrases.english: and I saw among them Jaazaniah son of Azzur

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת פְּלַטְיָהוּ בֶן בְּנָיָהוּ שָׂרֵי הָעָם״,
phrases.english: and Pelatiah son of Benaiah, officers of the people,"
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 11:1

phrases.english: And it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיָּבֹא אֹתִי אֶל חֲצַר בֵּית ה׳ הַפְּנִימִית
phrases.english: "And He brought me to the inner courtyard of the House of ה׳,
and behold, at the entrance of the Sanctuary of ה׳,
between the Hall and the Altar,
were about twenty-five men,
their backs toward the Sanctuary of ה׳
and their faces eastward."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 8:16

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר לְרָעָה, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the 'for good' story is finished, the גמרא turns to the source for the opposite view from Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'for bad' view connects פלטיהו to the twenty-five men who stood with their backs to the היכל.

steps.title: Reading 'their backs to the Sanctuary' as a disgraceful act
steps.stepSummary: Since 'faces eastward' already tells us their backs were to the west, the extra words 'backs to the היכל' must teach that they did a disgusting act toward ה׳. So the נביא asks: should such a person die peacefully in bed?
steps.simpleTranslation: Once the פסוק says 'their faces were eastward', don't I already know their backs were to the west? So why does it add 'their backs to the היכל of ה׳'? It teaches that they uncovered themselves and relieved themselves toward Above. And the נביא is saying: Should someone who did this evil in Israel die quietly in his bed?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the second פסוק shows that פלטיהו was wicked. The extra words are read as describing a terrible insult to the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the men face east, their backs are naturally to the west, where the היכל stood, so the words 'their backs to the היכל' seem extra. The גמרא says those words point to a shameful act aimed at the היכל. So in this view, יחזקאל's cry means 'such a sinner deserved to die', not 'what a loss'.

keyTerms.meaning: what does the פסוק come to teach (why the extra words)?

steps.whatToRemember: The two readings of יחזקאל's cry: 'for good' means פלטיהו was a hero who died too young. 'For bad' means he was one of the men who disgraced the היכל and deserved to die.

phrases.english: From the fact that it says, "and their faces eastward,"
don't I know that their backs were toward the west?
What does the verse teach by saying
"their backs toward the Sanctuary of ה׳"?
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording, so the quote matches the פסוק.

phrases.english: It teaches that they uncovered themselves
and relieved themselves toward Above.
And the prophet is saying:
One who did this evil in Israel,
should he die on his bed?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּשְׁמַע שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וּפְנֵיהֶם קֵדְמָה אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁאֲחוֹרֵיהֶם כְּלַפֵּי מַעֲרָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוקים quoted in Step 9 prove the 'for bad' reading.
steps.raayaObject: That פלטיהו was wicked and his death was a punishment.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra words 'their backs toward the היכל' in יחזקאל 8:16, together with יחזקאל 11:1 naming פלטיהו among the twenty-five.

steps.title: Proving that שמואל is the one who says 'for bad'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that the 'for bad' view belongs to שמואל. שמואל says מישן had no slavery problem in its lineage, so he cannot accept the story that slaves were sent there.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can conclude that it is שמואל who says 'for bad'. For רבי חייא בר אבין said in the name of שמואל: מושכני is like בבל in lineage. About מישן, there was no worry about slavery or ממזרות. The only problem was that the כהנים there were not careful to avoid divorced women.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 6 did not say which of רב and שמואל held which view. Here the גמרא tries to prove it from a separate statement of שמואל about the lineage of מישן. The next step pushes back on this proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'for good' story in Step 8 says slaves were sent to מישן. But שמואל says the people of מישן had no slavery concern at all. So it seems שמואל cannot hold the 'for good' story, which would mean he says 'for bad' and רב says 'for good'. The next step pushes back on this proof.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא tries to prove from שמואל's view on מישן's lineage that שמואל says 'for bad' and רב says 'for good'. The next step rejects this proof.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think שמואל says מישן is fully fine. He says it has no slavery or ממזרות problem, but it does have a כהונה problem, because כהנים there married divorced women.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the אגדה story back to the main topic of the פרק, which is the lineage of different places in בבל.

phrases.english: Conclude that it is Shmuel who said 'for bad,'

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: for Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Avin said that Shmuel said:
Mushkhenei is like the Exile with regard to lineage.
phrases.notes: 'The Exile' means the main Jewish area of בבל, whose families were known to have pure lineage.

phrases.english: Mishon: they were not concerned about it

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מִשּׁוּם עַבְדוּת וְלֹא מִשּׁוּם מַמְזֵרוּת,
phrases.english: neither because of slavery nor because of mamzer status,
rather, the priests who were there
were not careful about divorced women.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּסְתַּיֵּים דִּשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמַר לְרָעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the question of Step 6 (which אמורא held which view) by using a detail from the story in Step 8. Step 12 rejects the attempt.
steps.raayaObject: That שמואל is the one who reads יחזקאל's cry 'for bad'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's statement, said in his name by רבי חייא בר אבין, that מישן had no concern of slavery, which clashes with the story that slaves were sent there.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The proof suggests שמואל holds 'for bad' and רב holds 'for good', but step 12 rejects it, so the attribution is not settled.

steps.title: שמואל can still hold the 'for good' view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 11. שמואל could still say 'for good,' because he holds that a slave whose owner gives up ownership goes free without a document.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, I can tell you that שמואל said 'for good.' שמואל is following his own reasoning, because he said that if someone gives up ownership of his slave, the slave goes free and does not need a document of freedom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 11. שמואל might hold the 'for good' view after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said שמואל could not accept a story about slaves being sent to מישן, because that would damage מישן's lineage. The answer is that slaves whose masters stayed behind were effectively ownerless, so they became free. That means no slave problem ever entered מישן's lineage, and the story fits שמואל fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning that he uses elsewhere
A document that frees a slave

phrases.english: Actually, I can tell you
that שמואל said "for good,"
phrases.notes: This is the view from step 7 that יחזקאל's cry was a good thing said about פלטיהו.

phrases.english: and שמואל follows his own reasoning, for he said:
One who declares his slave ownerless —
the slave goes out to freedom
and does not need a document of freedom,

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 11 that the 'for bad' view must belong to שמואל.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that שמואל cannot accept the story of slaves sent to מישן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed the slaves stayed slaves. By שמואל's own rule, slaves whose master has no control over them go free.

steps.title: שמואל's source: a slave is only one under his master's control
steps.stepSummary: שמואל learns from the words 'slave of a man' that only a slave his master controls counts as a slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the פסוק says: 'Every slave of a man, bought with money.' Does it mean only a man's slave and not a woman's? No. It means a slave whose master has authority over him is called a slave. A slave whose master has no authority over him is not called a slave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the פסוק that שמואל uses for his rule about ownerless slaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'slave of a man' can't be excluding a woman's slave, since women can own slaves too. So the word 'man' must point to a master who actually controls the slave. Once the master lets go, the person is no longer a slave.
steps.whatToRemember: By שמואל's rule, the slaves sent away to מישן were free, so מישן has no slavery problem, and שמואל can hold the 'for good' view.

phrases.english: as it says: "Every slave of a man, bought with money,"
phrases.notes: שמות 12:44

phrases.english: A slave of a man and not a slave of a woman?
phrases.notes: This is asked to show it can't be right. A woman's slave is a real slave too.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: עֶבֶד שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְרַבּוֹ עָלָיו –
phrases.english: Rather: a slave whose master has authority over him —
is called a slave;
a slave whose master has no authority over him —
is not called a slave.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: כׇּל עֶבֶד אִישׁ מִקְנַת כָּסֶף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind שמואל's rule from step 12.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that an ownerless slave goes free without a document.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי מאיר; the חכמים presume all lands are fine
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the משנה's ranking of lands by lineage is only רבי מאיר's view. The חכמים presume every land has proper lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: This is the view of רבי מאיר. But the חכמים say: all lands are presumed to have proper lineage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה about the lineage of different lands and says whose opinion it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treated lands outside בבל as having doubtful lineage. שמואל says that is only רבי מאיר. The חכמים start from the opposite assumption: families in any land are presumed proper unless we know otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: In a presumption of, assumed to be

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the practical question in the next steps: can one marry a woman from a land outside בבל?

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
This is the view of Rabbi Meir,
phrases.notes: 'This' means the משנה that ranks the lands, treating only בבל as fully clean in lineage.

phrases.english: but the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אֲרָצוֹת בְּחֶזְקַת כְּשֵׁרוֹת הֵם עוֹמְדוֹת.
phrases.english: All lands stand in a presumption of proper lineage.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story of פלטיהו and goes back to the משנה about the lineage of lands.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה is רבי מאיר's view. The חכמים hold that all lands are presumed to have proper lineage.

steps.title: אמימר allows a marriage to a woman from מחוזא
steps.stepSummary: אמימר allowed רב הונא בר נתן to marry a woman from מחוזא, a place outside the clean-lineage area.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר permitted רב הונא בר נתן to marry a woman from מחוזא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story of a practical ruling. It is setting up רב אשי's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מחוזא was outside the borders of בבל that count for lineage. So allowing this marriage seems to rely on the חכמים's view from step 14 that all lands are presumed fine.

keyTerms.meaning: To marry, to take as a wife

phrases.english: Ameimar permitted
Rav Huna bar Natan
to marry a woman from Mechoza.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמֵּימָר שְׁרָא לֵיהּ לְרַב הוּנָא בַּר נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A practical case that seems to apply the חכמים's view from step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אמימר permitted marrying a woman from מחוזא.

steps.title: רב אשי: other study houses did not teach שמואל's statement
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges אמימר. If he relied on שמואל's statement, three major study houses did not teach it that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: What is your thinking? Is it because רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל that the משנה is רבי מאיר and the חכמים say all lands are presumed fine? But the study houses of רב כהנא, רב פפא and רב זביד did not teach it that way!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי questions the reason behind אמימר's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי guesses that אמימר relied on שמואל's statement from step 14. He attacks that basis: three important study houses did not have that version. So the ruling might rest on a shaky report.

keyTerms.meaning: What is your thinking, your reason?
But look, here is a problem
The study house, the school of
They taught, they had this version

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: מַאי דַּעְתָּיךְ –
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to him: What is your thinking?
That Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
This is the view of Rabbi Meir,
but the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אֲרָצוֹת בְּחֶזְקַת כְּשֵׁרוֹת הֵן עוֹמְדוֹת?
phrases.english: All lands are presumed to have proper lineage?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא בֵּי רַב כָּהֲנָא לָא מַתְנוּ הָכִי,
phrases.english: But the study house of Rav Kahana did not teach it this way,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵי רַב פָּפָּא לָא מַתְנוּ הָכִי,
phrases.english: and the study house of Rav Pappa did not teach it this way,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵי רַב זְבִיד לָא מַתְנוּ הָכִי!
phrases.english: and the study house of Rav Zevid did not teach it this way!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: מַאי דַּעְתָּיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the basis of אמימר's ruling in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's reliance on שמואל's statement from step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Three major study houses did not have that statement, so it is a weak basis for a practical ruling.

steps.title: אמימר keeps his ruling based on רב זביד of נהרדעא
steps.stepSummary: אמימר did not accept רב אשי's objection, because he had heard the ruling directly from רב זביד of נהרדעא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, he did not accept it from him, because he had heard it from רב זביד of נהרדעא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us אמימר stood by his ruling despite רב אשי's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's objection rested on study houses that did not teach שמואל's statement. אמימר had a direct tradition from רב זביד of נהרדעא, so the missing versions elsewhere did not change his mind.

keyTerms.meaning: נהרדעא, a major city of Torah learning in בבל

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two רב זביד's. The study house of רב זביד in step 16 did not teach שמואל's statement. אמימר heard it from a different person, רב זביד of נהרדעא.

phrases.english: Even so,
he did not accept it from him,
phrases.notes: אמימר did not accept רב אשי's objection.

phrases.english: because he had heard it
from Rav Zevid of Nehardea.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי לָא קַיבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge by explaining why אמימר kept his ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since three study houses did not teach שמואל's statement, אמימר should drop his ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: אמימר had heard it directly from רב זביד of נהרדעא, so he kept his ruling.

steps.title: Will ממזרים and נתינים be pure in the future?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records an argument. רבי יוסי says ממזרים and נתינים will be pure in the future; רבי מאיר says they will not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: ממזרים and נתינים will be pure in the time to come; these are the words of רבי יוסי. רבי מאיר says: they will not be pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with an argument about the future status of ממזרים and נתינים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Pure' here means their lineage problem will be removed. רבי יוסי says this will happen in the time to come, and רבי מאיר says it will not. The next steps show each side's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught, introduces a ברייתא
ממזרים, children of forbidden unions who may not marry into the community
נתינים, descendants of the גבעונים, also barred from marrying into the community

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Mamzerim and Nesinim
will be pure in the time to come,
phrases.notes: 'Pure' here means their lineage problem will be removed.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.
Rabbi Meir says: They will not be pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַמְזֵירֵי וּנְתִינֵי טְהוֹרִים לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to lineage: the future status of ממזרים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: they will be purified in the future. רבי מאיר: they will not.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's proof: 'I will sprinkle pure water on you'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי brings a פסוק in יחזקאל promising that ה׳ will purify the people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said to him: But has it not already been said: 'And I will sprinkle pure water on you, and you will be pure'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives a פסוק to support his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק promises a general purification of the people in the future. רבי יוסי reads it broadly enough to include the lineage problem of ממזרים.

keyTerms.meaning: But has it not already been said?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said to him:
But has it not already been said:
"And I will sprinkle pure water on you, and you will be pure"!
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 36:25

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוסי supports his view from step 18.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי's view that ממזרים will be purified.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: the פסוק only lists impurity and idols
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר points to the rest of the פסוק, which spells out what will be purified: impurities and idols, not ממזרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said to him: When it says 'from all your impurities and from all your idols,' it means only those, and not from ממזרות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר rejects רבי יוסי's proof using the next words of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק goes on to list specific things: impurities and idols. רבי מאיר argues that listing them limits the promise to those things. Lineage problems like ממזרות are not on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: The status of being a ממזר

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said to him:
When it says:
"From all your impurities and from all your idols" —
phrases.notes: These are the next words of the same פסוק in יחזקאל.

phrases.english: but not from mamzer status.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי מֵאִיר: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יוסי's proof from step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי יוסי's reading of the פסוק as a full purification.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק itself spells out what is purified, impurities and idols, which leaves out ממזרות.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: 'I will purify you' includes ממזרות
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי answers from the end of the פסוק. 'I will purify you' is an extra, general phrase that includes ממזרות too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said to him: When it says 'I will purify you,' you must say it means even from ממזרות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי defends his view against רבי מאיר's rejection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After listing impurities and idols, the פסוק adds the general words 'I will purify you.' רבי יוסי says these extra words must add something beyond the list, and that something is ממזרות. So the purification is complete.

keyTerms.meaning: You must say, it must mean

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי says ממזרים and נתינים will be purified in the future, from 'אטהר אתכם.' רבי מאיר limits the פסוק to impurity and idols.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said to him:
When it says: "I will purify you" —
phrases.notes: These are the closing words of the same פסוק.

phrases.english: you must say: even from mamzer status.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר: אֲטַהֵר אֶתְכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי מאיר's rejection in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading an extra general phrase as adding to the list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The listed impurities and idols limit the promise, so ממזרות is not included.
steps.terutzMaskana: The added words 'אטהר אתכם' widen the promise to include ממזרות.

steps.title: A verse about a ממזר in אשדוד seems to fit only רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the פסוק 'a ממזר shall dwell in אשדוד' fits רבי מאיר well, and asks how רבי יוסי explains it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for רבי מאיר: that is why the פסוק says, 'And a ממזר shall dwell in אשדוד.' But for רבי יוסי, what does 'And a ממזר shall dwell in אשדוד' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק that seems to show ממזרים will still exist in the future, which is a problem for רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר said ממזרים will not be purified, so a future verse that mentions a ממזר living in אשדוד fits him perfectly. רבי יוסי said ממזרים will become pure, so for him the verse looks out of place. The גמרא wants to know how רבי יוסי reads it.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (for one opinion, but not the other)
This is what is written: the פסוק fits this view
Ashdod, a city named in the פסוק
A child born from a forbidden relationship who may not marry into the regular community

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Meir,
this is what is written:
"And a mamzer shall dwell in Ashdod."
phrases.notes: זכריה 9:6

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Yosei,
what is "And a mamzer shall dwell in Ashdod"?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the back-and-forth about the פסוק in יחזקאל, the גמרא brings a new פסוק that seems to support רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's view that ממזרים will be purified in the future
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A prophecy about the future mentions a ממזר living in אשדוד, so ממזרים still seem to exist then.

steps.title: רב יוסף's translation reads the verse differently
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי can read the פסוק the way רב יוסף translated it: Israel will live safely in a land where they used to be like strangers.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יוסף translates it: The house of Israel will live securely in their land, where they used to be like strangers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יוסי by using רב יוסף's Aramaic translation, which does not talk about ממזרים at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this translation, the word ממזר is read as 'from a strange people' (מעם זר), describing how Israel once felt like foreigners in their own land. So the פסוק is a promise of safety, not a statement that ממזרים will still exist. The challenge against רבי יוסי falls away.

phrases.english: As Rav Yosef translates it:
The house of Israel will dwell in security
in their land, where they used to be like strangers.
phrases.notes: Some versions say דָּמוּ (round brackets); the corrected wording says דָּמַיִין (square brackets). Both mean 'were like.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִמְתַרְגֵּם רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the פסוק in זכריה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the verse so it no longer refers to ממזרים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק says real ממזרים will live in אשדוד in the future.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק describes Israel living safely in a land where they once felt like strangers.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the הלכה is like רבי יוסי, that ממזרים will be purified in the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling on the argument between רבי יוסי and רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After both sides brought their verses, שמואל decides in favor of רבי יוסי. So the accepted view is that in the future ממזרים and נתינים will be pure.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה is like רבי יוסי: ממזרים and נתינים will be purified in the future.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the argument from step 18 with a ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי: ממזרים and נתינים will be pure in the future.

steps.title: Without this ruling, אליהו would remove whole groups from us
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says that if not for שמואל's ruling, אליהו would come and pull out group after group of people with forbidden lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: If רב יהודה had not said in the name of שמואל that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, אליהו would come and take out from us group after group of chained-together people.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains how important שמואל's ruling is: without it, many families would be found to have forbidden lineage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף assumes there are many hidden ממזרים among the Jewish people. If they would not be purified, אליהו would expose them and separate them out in large groups. Because the הלכה is like רבי יוסי, they will be purified instead.

keyTerms.meaning: אליהו הנביא, who will come before the final redemption
Collars or chains, like those put on prisoners

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָאו דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
phrases.english: If not that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said
the halacha follows Rabbi Yosei,
Eliyahu would come
and remove from us group after group of chained ones.
phrases.notes: Literally 'necks, necks of collars,' picturing prisoners chained by the neck. He means large groups of people with forbidden lineage.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אִי לָאו דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on how much the ruling in step 24 matters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, the many hidden ממזרים will be purified and not exposed and separated by אליהו.

steps.title: May a גר marry a ממזרת? רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה argue
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי יוסי says a גר may marry a ממזרת, and רבי יהודה says he may not. It adds that a גר, a freed slave, and a חלל may all marry a כהן's daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A גר may marry a ממזרת; these are the words of רבי יוסי. רבי יהודה says: A גר may not marry a ממזרת. A גר, a freed slave, and a חלל are all permitted to marry the daughter of a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא with an argument about whether a גר may marry a ממזרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether a גר counts as part of the 'קהל' (congregation) that a ממזר may not marry into. רבי יוסי says he does not count, so he may marry a ממזרת; רבי יהודה says he does count, so he may not. The ברייתא also says these three types of men may marry a כהן's daughter.

keyTerms.meaning: A son of a כהן born from a marriage forbidden to a כהן; he loses כהונה status

steps.confusionAlert: This רבי יוסי argument is a new topic. It is about who a גר may marry today, not about ממזרים being purified in the future.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A convert may marry a mamzeret,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
A convert may not marry a mamzeret.

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד גֵּר אֶחָד עֶבֶד מְשׁוּחְרָר וְחָלָל
phrases.english: Whether a convert, a freed slave, or a chalal,
they are permitted to marry a kohen's daughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: גֵּר נוֹשֵׂא מַמְזֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new subject after the ruling and comment in steps 24 and 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: a גר may marry a ממזרת. רבי יהודה: he may not. A גר, a freed slave, and a חלל may marry a כהן's daughter.

steps.title: What is רבי יוסי's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי allows a גר to marry a ממזרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יוסי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source behind רבי יוסי's view. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says a ממזר may not enter 'the קהל of ה׳.' The גמרא wants to know why רבי יוסי thinks a גר is not included in that קהל.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for רבי יוסי's view that a גר may marry a ממזרת.

steps.title: Five mentions of 'congregation' are written
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer: the word קהל appears five times in the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: Five 'congregations' are written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to give רבי יוסי's reason by pointing out that the Torah says קהל five times. The explanation of how this count works continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah uses the word קהל five times in the verses about people who may not 'enter the קהל of ה׳‎.' רבי יוסי will build his proof from how these five are counted. Here the גמרא only names the starting point.

phrases.english: Five "congregations" are written.
phrases.notes: He means the word קהל appears five times in the Torah's verses about who may not 'enter the קהל of ה׳.'

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲמִשָּׁה קְהָלֵי כְּתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי's reason is based on the five times the word קהל is written in the Torah. The explanation continues in the next lines.
